heading.purpose: Page/section titles and every button label. Never used for body copy.

body.purpose: Row content, form values, descriptive text — everything not called out elsewhere.

mono.purpose: Room numbers, shift codes, time ranges — anywhere digits must align by width.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: The one shadow in the system, for things genuinely floating: modals, popovers, toasts, the print-preview sheet.

motion.name: ease-strong-out
motion.purpose: Strong ease-out for modal, popover, tooltip, and toast entrances/exits — the built-in CSS ease-out reads too weak at this panel size.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: The one sanctioned scale transform: :active feedback on every button. Never used for hover or entrance decoration.

motion.name: popover-in
motion.purpose: Trigger-anchored entrance for dropdown menus and tooltips.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Toast entrance from its fixed bottom-right anchor.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Highest-emphasis action that isn't the accent action — banner CTAs, confirm on routine dialogs.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.4rem; height:2.25rem; padding-inline:0.85rem; border-radius:0.5rem; font-family:'Archivo','Public Sans',sans-serif; font-size:0.8125rem; font-weight:600; white-space:nowrap; border:none; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 120ms ease, transform 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn:active { transform:scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary { background:#141414; color:#fff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#000; }

components.name: Accent Button
components.description: The "do the main thing" action — Add/Save/Configure/Print. Reached for most often.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.4rem; height:2.25rem; padding-inline:0.85rem; border-radius:0.5rem; font-family:'Archivo','Public Sans',sans-serif; font-size:0.8125rem; font-weight:600; white-space:nowrap; border:none; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 120ms ease, transform 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn:active { transform:scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-accent { background:#1f6b4c; color:#fff; } .ds-btn-accent:hover { background:#1a5c40; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Cancel, Back, and other non-primary actions that still need a real button.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.4rem; height:2.25rem; padding-inline:0.85rem; border-radius:0.5rem; font-family:'Archivo','Public Sans',sans-serif; font-size:0.8125rem; font-weight:600; white-space:nowrap; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 120ms ease, transform 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn:active { transform:scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary { background:#ffffff; color:#141414; border:1px solid #ece8dc; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:#f5f2e9; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Reserved for real identity/state — Demo, Active, In Hospital, a category tag. Never decoration.
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; height:1.25rem; padding-inline:0.4rem; border-radius:0.2rem; font-family:'Public Sans',sans-serif; font-size:0.6875rem; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.02em; text-transform:uppercase; line-height:1; } .ds-badge-accent { background:#e8f2ec; color:#1a5c40; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The default "this is a distinct section" treatment — flat, no shadow, hierarchy from the hairline border only.

narrative.overview:
TaskSheet's screen UI plays a supporting role to the artifact staff actually carry away from it: a printed paper worksheet. The system reads like the working documents of a well-run nursing unit — a dark navy rail as fixed structural chrome (the binder's spine), a warm cream working surface (the paper itself), flat hairline-bordered panels (never an elevated card), one confident forest-green accent for anything interactive, and numeral-led identifiers (room, shift code, time) set apart in a mono face so they scan instantly down a column. Nothing competes for attention with the task at hand; the interface is built to disappear into the workflow, not to be evaluated on its own.

This is at least the third named visual direction this codebase has shipped — an earlier teal "Field Blueprint+" pass was superseded by a deliberate revert back toward TaskSheet's original navy-and-green identity. This document describes the system as it is actually built today, in src/index.css's own words: "navy rail / forest accent."
keyCharacteristics: Flat, hairline-bordered panels — never a floating card
One accent color, reserved for "interactive or selected," never decoration
Dense, numeral-forward typography for anything tabular
Motion limited to subtle press/entrance feedback — never lift, bounce, or attention-seeking movement
Desktop-first density tuned for a single nursing-station workstation, not a marketing surface

rules.name: The One Border Rule
rules.body: hairline and hairline-strong resolve to the identical #ece8dc — this system uses exactly one border weight everywhere. There is no heavier structural weight layered on top.

rules.name: The Unified Accent Rule
rules.body: --color-accent and --color-positive share the same forest-green hex (#1f6b4c). A resident marked Active and a button inviting a click read as the same color family on purpose.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight and structure more than size — a bold 13px row title next to a regular 13px metadata line reads clearly without a large size jump.

rules.name: The Flat-Card Rule
rules.body: A panel's hierarchy comes from its hairline border, never a shadow. Never add elevation to something that isn't actually floating.

rules.name: The AA-Over-Distinction Rule
rules.body: --color-faint (#6a6d64) and --color-muted (#6b6f76) sit close together on purpose: on a light panel, meaningfully lighter than Muted and still WCAG-AA-passing don't coexist in this hue. Correctness wins over a wider visual gap between the two de-emphasized tokens.

dos: Do route every color through the design tokens — never a raw Tailwind palette class or an arbitrary hex in screen UI.
Do use CardNavigationButton for any fully-clickable row/card — a real sibling button, never a nested interactive control.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus ring.
Do communicate status with a text label, never color alone.
Do keep the print document system on its own Arial/Helvetica typography contract — never "fix" it toward the screen fonts.
donts: Don't nest panels inside panels — use an internal divider instead.
Don't use rounded-xl/rounded-2xl/rounded-full outside a genuine pill/circular element.
Don't add a shadow to a surface that isn't genuinely floating.
Don't add hover-lift, bounce, or other attention-seeking motion — only the button press-scale and the modal/popover/toast entrances are sanctioned.
Don't give two buttons doing the same conceptual job different colors.
Don't invent a sixth badge color.
